justifications.functional_suitability: Requirements R-01 to R-03 are addressed by Media Gateway, E-Prescription Service, and AI Symptom Checker Container. However, patient-facing consent management (R-04) lacks an explicit management component, although enforcement is thoroughly handled by Consent Enforcement Proxy.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adaptive Bitrate & Congestion Controller manages dynamic bandwidth allocation. Outbox Worker & DLQ enables asynchronous processing, and Regional Caches ensure low-latency local evaluations. Specific audio-only degradation mechanisms under 300 kbit/s are not explicitly detailed.
justifications.compatibility: The Interoperability Adapter uses an Adapter Plugins & Strategy Pattern to cleanly support US HL7 FHIR and diverse EU national standards, integrating effectively with Regional Pharmacies and National Standards APIs.
justifications.usability: Patients and Licensed Clinicians are represented, but no client-side user interfaces (web or mobile applications) are modeled. While Media Gateway mitigates connection issues for rural users, direct interaction with backend gateways overlooks client UX needs.
justifications.reliability: Unstable rural connections are mitigated by TURN/STUN Relay Handler and GCC adaptive bitrate control. E-prescription dispatch reliability is reinforced by Outbox Worker & DLQ, though automated cross-region database failover mechanisms are omitted.
justifications.security: Data residency across europe-west3 and us-central1 is strictly maintained. Consent Enforcement Proxy uses OPA and token revocation checks for cross-region access, while Audit Logging and Compliance Validator ensure HIPAA, GDPR, and MDR traceability.
justifications.maintainability: Clean separation of concerns with package-per-country strategy in Interoperability Adapter, sidecar-based OPA Policy Engine, decoupled configuration services, and comprehensive OpenTelemetry instrumentation promote exceptional maintainability and testability.
justifications.portability: The architecture aligns with target GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1). Standard technologies like OPA, OpenTelemetry, Coturn, and Janus offer high portability, though reliance on GCP-specific configurations slightly limits effortless provider migration.

PERF-01.justification: Media Gateway separates Janus signaling and Coturn relay, but lacks explicit horizontal auto-scaling and load-distribution mechanisms necessary for 5,000 concurrent media streams.
sensitivity_points: Signaling throughput and concurrent relay capacity of Janus and Coturn nodes
tradeoffs: Relaying media through dedicated proxies enhances NAT traversal but increases bandwidth and CPU overhead

PERF-02.justification: Handling ~14 requests/second via gRPC dispatch and Redis-backed session caching comfortably meets the sub-3s latency threshold under peak conditions.
sensitivity_points: In-memory Redis lookup and gRPC processing efficiency
tradeoffs: Asynchronous logging reduces response latency but defers log persistence guarantees

AVAIL-01.justification: The Adaptive Bitrate and Congestion Controller using GCC paired with Coturn fallback ensures degraded streaming under 300 kbit/s, though note synchronization reliability is implicit.
sensitivity_points: Responsiveness of Google Congestion Control to rapid bandwidth drops
tradeoffs: Lowering video bitrate preserves connection stability at the cost of visual fidelity

AVAIL-02.justification: Only us-central1 is provisioned in the US; no secondary US region or automated multi-region DR exists to restore service while preserving US data residency.
sensitivity_points: Lack of a redundant US cloud region to satisfy residency constraints
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents active failover to EU infrastructure during regional outages

MOD-01.justification: The Interoperability Adapter explicitly employs a package-per-country Strategy pattern with schema validation and dynamic feature flagging, confining changes entirely to one adapter.
sensitivity_points: Strict decoupling of national adapter plugins from core prescription workflows
tradeoffs: Pluggable strategy pattern introduces abstraction layers but prevents country-specific core modifications

MOD-02.justification: Feature flags enable controlled rollout and instant rollback of model versions, while Audit Event Emitter logs inputs and versions, though model retraining pipelines are unstated.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic runtime propagation of feature flag configurations to AI dispatchers
tradeoffs: Logging full input payloads ensures MDR traceability but increases storage consumption

SEC-01.justification: The Consent Enforcement Proxy intercepts cross-region traffic, validates tokens against Bloom filters and Redis, evaluates OPA Rego policies, and triggers immutable audit logging.
sensitivity_points: Correctness and latency of real-time OPA evaluation on cross-region calls
tradeoffs: In-line cross-region policy checks ensure compliance but introduce round-trip evaluation latency

SEC-02.justification: Consent revocation is dynamically validated for API requests using Bloom filters and Redis, but downstream data deletion or research data segregation pipelines are missing.
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of token revocation state across regional Bloom filters
tradeoffs: Immediate access revocation via sidecar avoids batch delays but does not purge persisted data
